# Assumption of Moses Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Latin palimpsest (Codex Ambrosianus) | **Section:** Moses' Farewell Commission to Joshua

---

**1** The testament of Moses, which he made in the one hundred and twentieth year of his life, which is the two thousand five hundredth year from the creation of the world, in the one hundred and twentieth year after the departure from Phoenicia, when the people went out after the exodus accomplished by Moses from Egypt.

**2** According to the number of years written in the covenant, after Moses had received authority through his prophecy from God, and after the departure of the children of Israel — according to Moses speaking from a book, in the fortieth year in the wilderness.

**3** Moses called Joshua the son of Nun to himself and said to him:

**4** Give heed to all that I tell you now, Joshua son of Nun; for God chose me for his people in order to make the covenant with them and to be mediator of the covenant.

**5** From the beginning of the world even to the end of time, Moses was prepared to be the mediator of the covenant of God.

**6** And the Lord said to me: I have appointed you from the beginning of the world to be the mediator of the covenant.

**7** Receive these writings, so that you may know how to preserve the books which I shall deliver to you.

**8** You shall arrange them, anoint them with cedar oil, and deposit them in earthen vessels in the place which he prepared from the beginning of the creation of the world.

**9** For this shall be the testimony of God.

**10** For behold, God has appointed me to pray on behalf of their sins and to make intercession for them.

**11** Not because of any virtue of mine or the strength of my arms, but because of his compassion and his patience he has nourished them.

**12** For thus says the Lord of the world: he created the world on behalf of his people but did not make this purpose known from the beginning of the world,

**13** so that the nations might be convicted by their own evil and humiliated through the nations of his own making, that his purpose might be made manifest.

**14** Yes, he devised and planned on their behalf, and he prepared and appointed me from the beginning of the world to be the mediator of his covenant.

**15** And now I am about to go the way of sleep with my fathers, and you shall go in to the land which he has prepared for them.
